body:
why would you want this? then autoload scenes wouldnt be able to use those resources, and the only "upside" to this would be that you could abuse the hell out of autoload scenes for what clearly should be the job of something - *anything* - else. the solution here is obvious: dont access the autoload from before its loaded.

if you want a singleton, make an actual singleton, eg using `static`. not an additional main scene with a global name. if you want projectsettings, use projectsettings. not an additional main scene with a global name. it's not hard not to abuse autoloads for everything.

Autoloads exist to be global singletons within, primarily, the scope of the scenetree. The further you stray from that, the more likely you will be burned.

This is a consequence of bad architecture, not a problem to be solved. Resources are already not really supposed to have references into the scenetree, much less a global instance. I assure you, godot is not so completely incompetent that your hand is twisted in this scenario. I am confident there is a way to accomplish your goals in a manner far less inane.

@nonchip @UwUMacaroniTime  

This problem goes beyond `ResourceFormatLoaders` and `ResourceFormatSavers`  themselves. If I have some class named `ExampleLoader` that extends `ResouceFormatLoader` then ANY classes referenced by `ExampleLoader` for example `ExampleResource` and cannot contain a reference to a autoload singleton. This is a recursive property.

The MRP I provided is simply the most trivial implementation capable of triggering this error. In real world projects (such as my own) this error can be far more insidious and can appear when adding a reference to an autoload singleton to a class seemingly unrelated to  `ResourceFormatLoaders` or `ResourceFormatSavers` .

For example, in my actual project I have a custom `ResourceFormatLoader` I'll call `ExampleLoader` which loads a custom resource called `ExampleResource`. This `ExampleResource` has a method which allows me to create a custom node I'll call `ExamplePlayerNode` using the contents of the resource. This seems architecturally reasonable to me and works without issue. I've even seen a few Godot tutorials recommending something like this.

```
# Example class reference hierarchy
ExampleLoader -> ExampleResource -> ExamplePlayerNode -> ExampleWeaponNode -> Autoload
```

However, if I were to then add a reference to an autoload singleton to `ExamplePlayerNode` or even to a class referenced by `ExamplePlayerNode` such as `ExampleWeaponNode`. I'd trigger this bug and encounter a `Identifier not found: Autoload` error, despite that fact that `ExampleLoader` never calls any code related to `ExamplePlayerNode` or `ExampleWeaponNode` let alone the `Autoload` itself.

I completely agree that autoload singletons have no business anywhere in a `ResourceFormatLoaders` or `ResourceFormatSavers`  class or even a `Resource` for that matter. But adding a reference to a seemingly unrelated class should at least trigger a more fitting error message then `Identifier not found: Autoload`.

I'd be happy to provide a more detailed project file than the MRP that shows how this bug can arise in a more complex environment such as the one described here.

Perhaps a better fix would be to register autoload singletons to the language server first. Then load all custom  `ResourceFormatLoaders` and `ResourceFormatSavers` then load the autoload singletons themselves. This might fix the issue without breaking the use of custom resources in autoload singletons.
